summary: An L-4 ground cab moved from the Fairchild Point tower in 1952; unstaffed since the 1970s, now a roadside overlook with a view of the Imnaha River in Wallowa County.

facts.design: Standard US Forest Service L-4 ground cabin and catwalk on short stone aggregate piers; cab moved from the Fairchild Point tower
facts.status_note: Not used as a fire lookout since the 1970s; the cab still stands at Buckhorn Overlook.

access.note: Roadside overlook on National Forest land, reached by road. The 2022 register visit found the door open, shutters missing and glass on the floor. A 2023 visit found the lookout and garage still standing but slowly crumbling.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest

events.note: Cab lowered from the Fairchild Point tower and moved to this site as the new lookout for the Chesnimus District; original construction date unknown
Last year on firelookout.com's list of known lookout personnel; the page says the cab was last staffed in the 1970s
Register visit report (October 1, 2022): needs paint, shutters missing, door open, glass on floor, number of broken windows unknown
Registered June 22, 2022 as US 1609, OR 136; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.current: 1952 built ('Built' field on NHLR detail page)
corrections.proposed: 1952 relocated (cab moved here from the Fairchild Point tower; original construction date unknown)
corrections.why: The register's Built field reads 'Relocated 1952' and says the original construction date is unknown; the 1952 event was a move, not a build.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1954 forest history, as quoted by Forest Lookouts, calls the new site Buckhorn Point; the register and firelookout.com use Buckhorn Mountain; Every Lookout in Oregon calls it Buckhorn Overlook today and found no official name.

notes_for_editor: Record says 1952 built; the register says Relocated 1952 with unknown original construction date (correction proposed). Status is standing as a physical cab but abandoned as a lookout (facts.status). Elevation: 1,628 m on the register matches the record; feet differ (5,341 ft register, 5,331 ft firelookout.com and Every Lookout in Oregon, 5,333 ft in a 2017 hiking blog not used as a source). Staffing list from firelookout.com names individuals; the story omits names. Access: the cab is reached from a roadside overlook on National Forest land; the 2022 register notes (open door, glass on floor) are the only interior condition record, and the story does not advise on entering. No notable fire, no rental and no restoration appear in the sources reviewed. Confidence high on the 1952 move; the parking and road access rest on a 2023 visit account.
